subject: Social Habits
title: Being kind
objectives: Children will use gentle hands with friends and toys.
Children will say a kind word or help a friend.
content: Kind hands, kind words and helping a friend.
teachingActivities: Teach "gentle hands" with a soft toy; notice and name every kind act ("You helped Ada, that was kind"); never label a child as unkind; show kind words with a puppet; use a kindness chart with stickers.
learnerActivities: Use gentle hands, say a kind word and help a friend with support.
assessment: Observe whether each child uses gentle hands and says or does a kind thing with support.
expectedOutcomes: Uses gentle hands with a friend.
Says or does a kind thing with support.

lessons.title: Kind hands
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will use gentle hands with a soft toy and a friend.
successCriteria: Uses gentle hands with a friend with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can share and take turns with support.
lessons.starter: Hold a soft toy gently and say "I use kind hands. I do not hit or push."
teacherActivities: Show how to stroke a soft toy gently.
Say "Kind hands help. Kind hands share."
Let children pat a friend’s hand gently if they wish.
Use the puppet to show what happens if hands are not kind.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to stroke a soft toy gently. Children: Children copy the gentle touch.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Kind hands help. Kind hands share." Children: Children look at their hands.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children pat a friend’s hand gently if they wish. Children: Child pats a friend’s hand.
Step 4. Teacher: Use the puppet to show what happens if hands are not kind. Children: Children say gentle.

practical.title: Gentle hands
practical.safety: Never force touch. Let children choose a wave or high five instead. Stay close to children who hit or push and gently redirect them.

differentiation.support: Guide the child’s hand gently on the soft toy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show a friend gentle hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says gentle or kind with support
lessons.homeConnection: Praise your child for gentle hands and show how to be gentle with a baby or a pet.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use gentle hands with a soft toy and a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Kind hands, kind hands, help and share.

lessons.title: Kind words
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say a kind word to a friend.
successCriteria: Says a kind word with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can share and take turns with support.
lessons.starter: Let the puppet say "You are my friend" and give a big smile.
teacherActivities: Show kind words: hello, well done, thank you, you are my friend.
Use the puppet to say a kind word to a child.
Let each child say a kind word to a friend.
Add a sticker to the kindness chart.
learnerActivities: Child smiles or says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show kind words: hello, well done, thank you, you are my friend. Children: Children say the words.
Step 2. Teacher: Use the puppet to say a kind word to a child. Children: Child smiles or says thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child say a kind word to a friend. Children: Child says a kind word.
Step 4. Teacher: Add a sticker to the kindness chart. Children: Child places a sticker.

practical.title: Kind words round
steps: Say a kind word to a friend.
Add a sticker to the chart.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic stickers and watch that none are put in mouths. Never force a child to speak; accept a smile.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say a kind word to every friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who do you say it to?

expectedOutcomes: Says a kind word with a prompt
Smiles when saying a kind word
lessons.conclusion: Say "You are kind" to a friend.
lessons.homeConnection: Use kind words with your child and ask them to say one to a family member.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say a kind word to a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Helping a friend
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will help a friend in a simple way.
successCriteria: Helps a friend pick up something
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can share and take turns with support.
lessons.starter: Let the puppet drop its bag and say "Oh no! Who can help me?"
teacherActivities: Show how to pick up the bag and give it back.
Let each child help the puppet or a friend pick up toys.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to pick up the bag and give it back. Children: Children watch and help.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "We help our friends." Children: Children repeat help.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child help the puppet or a friend pick up toys. Children: Child picks up toys.
Step 4. Teacher: Say thank you to helpers. Children: Children say you are welcome.

practical.title: Helping hands
steps: Children help to pick them up.
practical.safety: Use light, large objects and keep the floor clear. Supervise carefully so no child is hurt while helping.

differentiation.support: Help together and hold the object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend who needs help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do for friends?

expectedOutcomes: Helps a friend in a simple way
lessons.conclusion: Look at the helpful class and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to help with a small job and say thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help a friend in a simple way" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Kindness every day
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will use kind hands, kind words and helping in play.
successCriteria: Uses a kind action in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can share and take turns with support.
lessons.starter: Show the kindness chart and say "When we are kind, we get a sticker."
teacherActivities: Watch children play and name kind acts you see.
Say "I saw you share. That was kind."
Let children say a kind thing they did.
learnerActivities: Child smiles and receives a sticker.
Child says or shows what they did.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Watch children play and name kind acts you see. Children: Children play together.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "I saw you share. That was kind." Children: Child smiles and receives a sticker.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children say a kind thing they did. Children: Child says or shows what they did.
Step 4. Teacher: Count the stickers together. Children: Children count with support.

practical.title: Kindness spotting
practical.safety: Give praise for kind acts and never remove a sticker. Use non-toxic stickers and supervise play.

differentiation.support: Name a kind act the child did and give a sticker.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to spot a kind act by a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What did you do that was kind?

expectedOutcomes: Uses a kind action in play
Says a kind thing they did
lessons.homeConnection: Notice and praise your child’s kind acts at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use kind hands, kind words and helping in play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 kindness check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child shows kindness.
successCriteria: Says or does a kind thing
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can share and take turns with support.
lessons.starter: Sing the kind hands song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: gentle hands, kind words and helping.
At each station watch how the child shows kindness.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: gentle hands, kind words and helping. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child shows kindness. Children: Child plays with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Kindness stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and step in gently if a child is rough. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend how to help.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: uses gentle hands; says a kind word; helps a friend; plays kindly with others.

questions.question: What do we do for friends?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep praising kind acts at home.
